ArgumentAgainst:
The sales tax is too high. If this measure passes, Tacoma purchases will incur a tax of 10.8%; for vehicles: 11.3%.  Does anyone think this is the best rate?  No.  It's too high.

Pierce Transit asked people if they want more service.  They want more service.  They don't want higher sales taxes, because everyone knows they're too high.

Higher sales taxes hit the poor hardest.  Higher rates lead to greater tax avoidance, and the rich use workarounds (driving out of the district or paying cash under the table).  Such avoidance reduces funding for other services, all because the sales tax is too high.

The House Transportation Committee Chair represents the heart of our service area.  We should all ask him to identify another funding source. Because the sales tax is too high.
ArgumentFor:
Dignity for those who can't drive
For many people, transit is the difference between reaching a job, a medical appointment, or the grocery store, and not reaching it at all. When transit is lacking, riders with disabilities, older adults, and workers suffer. They waste hours waiting and miss opportunities. No one should have to work twice as hard to live their life just because they can't drive.

Investing in more options, less traffic
For just 3 cents on a $10 purchase, Proposition 1 funds the first local transit investment since 2002. A "yes" vote will bring more bus routes, running more often, at more times of day, with better connections to light rail and Sounder. It will increase service county-wide by 47%, connect people to jobs and affordable housing, and improve traffic.

Free fares for seniors and youth
Proposition 1 makes transit free for seniors and protects free youth fares, helping seniors age with grace and stay independent, while helping young people get to school and jobs.
BallotTitle:
The Board of Commissioners of the Pierce County Public Transportation Benefit Area, commonly known as Pierce Transit, adopted Resolution No. 2026-006 concerning a sales and use tax for local transportation services.

This proposition would authorize the collection of an additional sales and use tax of three-tenths of one percent, or three pennies for every $10 spent, to maintain and improve transit service, including adding bus routes and special event service; expanding daytime, evening, and weekend service; reducing wait times between buses; improving access to light rail, healthcare, schools, and jobs; expanding service for people with disabilities; and providing fare-free bus service to seniors and youth, effective April 1,

ExplanatoryStatement:
This proposition, if passed, would provide exclusive, direct support for Pierce County bus and transit services by authorizing an additional 3/10th of 1% (0.3%) sales and use tax, equivalent to 3 cents on a $10 taxable purchase.

The proposition would fund the preservation and expansion of transportation services throughout Pierce Transit’s service area. Planned improvements would reduce wait times and improve access to schools, healthcare, shopping, job centers, light rail, and community events by adding new bus routes, increasing how frequently buses arrive, and expanding evening and weekend bus service.

Funding would also support services for people with disabilities, commuter vanpools connecting employees to work, and partnerships to help students travel safely. Additional funding would support seasonal and special event services to destinations like fairs, festivals, sports events, and waterfront access. The funding would also support fare-free bus service for seniors and continued free transit for youth.

Pierce Transit is operating at the maximum level current funding allows and despite rising costs has not received a sales tax rate increase since 2002. Sales tax revenues account for approximately 80% of the operating budget. If rejected, Pierce Transit would begin planning service reductions due to rising costs. Learn more at www.piercetransit.org.
RebuttalAgainst: Even opponents admit we need more transit service. Transit funding hasn't increased since 2002, and working families are paying the price. Under state law, the sales tax is Pierce Transit's only funding option — there is no other source. It isn't charged on groceries, rent, or medicine. This measure makes fares free for seniors and keeps them free for youth. It puts transit where it's needed most. Join your neighbors, labor unions, and businesses: vote yes.
RebuttalFor: The “for” statement is 100% correct.  I ride transit to work (where I collect sales taxes).  I’m frustrated that there’s no service early Sunday to get me to church.  My life is greatly impacted by the existence and shortcomings of transit, as are the lives of many others.  But higher sales tax is no way to fund it.  Demand better!
